# Data

------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r}
# samples
sp <- read_csv(file.path(cfg$project$data,"imagery_zooscan_samples+acquisitions_cleaned.csv")) 

# marine regions and daytime
mr <- read_csv(file.path(cfg$project$data,"imagery_zooscan_samples_marine_regions+daytime.csv")) %>% 
  # one summer Arctic sample is missing a day value
  mutate(day_night=if_else(sampleid==378000027,"Day",day_night))

# objects
obj <- read_csv(file.path(cfg$project$data,"imagery_zooscan_objects_morpho_taxo_cleaned.csv")) %>% 
  select(objid,sampleid,acquisid,grey_median,grey_std,
         scientificname:family_order) %>% 
  left_join(distinct(sp,sampleid,genid,acquisid,d,date,latitude,longitude)) %>% 
  left_join(distinct(mr,genid,ocean_seas,longhurstabb,longhurst,day_night,biome)) 
```

Let's calculate the average median organism transparency per sample:

```{r}
sp_mean <- obj %>% 
  group_by(genid,date,latitude,longitude,ocean_seas,longhurstabb,longhurst,day_night,biome) %>% 
  summarize(gmedian=sum(grey_median*d)/sum(d))
```

# Ocean basins

## Statistics

### Hypothesis

For the average transparency per sample (not the distribution of transparency at the organism level), all oceans have a normal distribution of samples, except for the Northern Atlantic (but W close to 1 and p-value of 0.02 so minor deviation).

We also fail to reject the null hypothesis of equal variance so we can assume that they are indeed homogeneous.

```{r}
# normality: Shapiro-Wilk test
for (i in unique(sp_mean$ocean_seas)){
  print(i)
  print(shapiro.test(sp_mean$gmedian[sp_mean$ocean_seas==i]))
}

# variance
leveneTest(gmedian ~ ocean_seas, data = sp_mean)
#bartlett.test(gmedian ~ ocean_seas, data = sp_mean)
```

### Tests

Since normality and homogeneity of variance: there are significant differences in the mean between the different oceans/seas.

```{r}
# one-way ANOVA
anova_result <- aov(gmedian ~ ocean_seas, data = sp_mean)
summary(anova_result)
# kruskal.test(gmedian ~ ocean_seas, data = sp_mean)

# pairwise test: Tukey
tukey_result <- TukeyHSD(anova_result)
print(tukey_result)

tukey_tidy <- tidy(tukey_result) %>% 
  mutate(p.adj.signif = case_when(
    adj.p.value < 0.001 ~ "***",
    adj.p.value < 0.01 ~ "**",
    adj.p.value < 0.05 ~ "*",
    TRUE ~ "ns"
  )) %>% 
  arrange(adj.p.value) %>% 
  select(-c(term,null.value)) %>% 
  mutate(term1=str_split_i(contrast,"-",1),
         term2=str_split_i(contrast,"-",2))
tukey_tidy

library(ggplot2)

# Plot the differences and confidence intervals
ggplot(tukey_tidy, aes(x = reorder(term2,estimate), y = estimate)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = p.adj.signif)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), width = 0.2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  facet_wrap(.~term1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("ns" = "black", "*" = "blue", "**" = "green", "***" = "purple")) +
  labs(
    x = "Group Comparison",
    y = "Difference in Means",
    title = "Tukey's HSD: Pairwise Differences with Significance"
  ) +
  coord_flip() + 
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
 # distribution per ocean 
ocean_indiv_mean <- obj %>% group_by(ocean_seas) %>% 
  summarize(moy=sum(grey_median*d)/sum(d),
            std = sqrt(sum(d * (grey_median - moy)^2) / sum(d))) %>% arrange(moy) %>%
  mutate(ocean_seas = str_remove(ocean_seas, "\\s+\\w+$")) %>%
  mutate(ocean_seas = factor(ocean_seas, levels = unique(tot_mean$ocean_seas)))
ocean_indiv_mean

densities <- obj %>%
  mutate(ocean_seas = str_remove(ocean_seas, "\\s+\\w+$")) %>%
  mutate(ocean_seas = factor(ocean_seas, levels = unique(tot_mean$ocean_seas))) %>%
  group_by(ocean_seas) %>%
  summarise(density_data = list({
    subset_data <- grey_median
    subset_weights <- d
    subset_weights <- subset_weights / sum(subset_weights, na.rm = TRUE)

    # Compute weighted mean and sd
    wmean <- sum(subset_data * subset_weights)
    wvar <- sum(subset_weights * (subset_data - wmean)^2)
    wsd <- sqrt(wvar)

    # Use this to estimate bandwidth (rule-of-thumb style)
    bw <- 1.06 * wsd * length(subset_data)^(-1/5)

    dens <- density(subset_data, weights = subset_weights, bw = bw, n = 512)
    tibble(x = dens$x, y = dens$y)
  }), .groups = "drop") %>%
  unnest(density_data)


dist_oceans <- ggplot(densities, aes(x = x, y = ocean_seas, height = y, fill = ocean_seas)) +
  geom_ridgeline(scale = 40, alpha = 0.7) +  # scale to amplify vertical height
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "North Atlantic" = "#004C99",
    "South Atlantic" = "#66A9FF",
    "North Pacific" = "#007D71",
    "South Pacific" = "#4DC3AD",
    "Arctic" = "#505050",
    "Southern" = "#A9A9A9",
    "Indian" = "#FF6F61",
    "Mediterranean" = "#F4A736"
  )) +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x = "Organism transparency", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", text = element_text(size = 12))
dist_oceans
```

# Day night

## Statistics

### Hypothesis

The day samples are not normally distributed (p=0.005) and there isn't homogeneity of variance.

```{r}
# normality: Shapiro-Wilk test
for (i in unique(sp_mean$day_night)){
  print(i)
  print(shapiro.test(sp_mean$gmedian[sp_mean$day_night==i]))
}

# variance
leveneTest(gmedian ~ day_night, data = sp_mean)
#bartlett.test(gmedian ~ ocean_seas, data = sp_mean)
```

### Tests

Night samples are not normal through Shapiro, so we will run a Mann-Whitney U test (Wilcoxon Rank-Sum test).

```{r}
wilcox.test(gmedian ~ day_night, data = sp_mean, alternative = "two.sided")
```

What about day/night per ocean?

```{r}
# how many samples 
count(ungroup(sp_mean),day_night,ocean_seas) %>% arrange(ocean_seas,n)

# day night differences
daynight_diff <- sp_mean %>% 
  group_by(ocean_seas,day_night) %>% 
  summarize(moy=mean(gmedian)) %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from="day_night",values_from="moy") %>% 
  mutate(difference=Day-Night)

# two-way ANOVA 
mod <- aov(gmedian ~ day_night * ocean_seas,
  data = sp_mean)

# print results
summary(mod)

# linear model
model <- lm(
  gmedian ~ ocean_seas * day_night,
  data = sp_mean
)
summary(model)

# adjusted
library(emmeans)
emmeans(
  model,
  pairwise ~ day_night | ocean_seas,
  adjust = "BH"
)
```

# Biomes

## Statistics

### Hypothesis

The coastal and westerlies biomes are not normal and there isn't homogeneity of variance.

```{r}
# normality: Shapiro-Wilk test
for (i in unique(sp_mean$biome)){
  print(i)
  print(shapiro.test(sp_mean$gmedian[sp_mean$biome==i]))
}

# variance
leveneTest(gmedian ~ biome, data = sp_mean)
#bartlett.test(gmedian ~ ocean_seas, data = sp_mean)
```

### Tests

Do a a Kruskal-Wallis (does not assume normality), and Games-Howell for post-hoc comparisons (robust to unequal variances).

```{r}
# Kruskal-Wallis
kruskal.test(gmedian ~ biome, data = sp_mean)

# Games-Howell
library(rstatix)
games_howell_test(data = ungroup(sp_mean) %>% mutate(biome=factor(biome)), formula = gmedian ~ biome) %>% arrange(p.adj)
pairwise.wilcox.test(sp_mean$gmedian, sp_mean$biome, p.adjust.method = "BH")
```
